view.text: Berth four. The Patience knocks the pilings. The shack window is lit. The lane home is a guess in the fog.
The ledger is in your coat. The lane, with the book shut, climbs to the office. Hold it open only to spend the hour on the dock.
view.holding: Tonight's tide is circled beside his name. The face under the pilings is that name.
His name, and an hour already passed. The lane would carry it to a dry room.

location.asset: You kneel at the edge. Between the pilings something pale turns, the size of a face, and the tide takes it.
You look again. The harbor keeps what it turned. The name is in the book, not in the tide.
You take the lane with the book shut. The fog lets you pass. The town begins where the planks end.
Marsh puts a palm between the ledger and the deck. "Dry room," he says. "Her voice waiting. Not this boat, and not this fog."
location.ending: You read his hour to the harbor. The pale face turns up between the pilings and does not go back under.
You take the lane with empty hands. The fog lets you go. In the morning the folder is still on the desk, and Thomas Voss is a wet line on a washed board.
location.asset: Marsh turns his clear eye on you and his clouded one on the shack.

view.text: Marsh keeps his clear eye on you and the clouded one on the shack. He knows why you are here. He waits to see which question you start with.
view.holding: Dry room. Her voice waiting. Not this boat, and not this fog.

view.text: Marsh does not turn. He has said what he has to say, but he will answer what is asked.
view.holding: Dry room. Her voice waiting. Not this boat, and not this fog.

location.asset: "He kept the tide. He came down for his hour and did not come up." He nods at the shack without looking at it. "Nothing went in the water from this deck."
"The book is on the table. Leave the floor. Read the hour to the woman up the hill." He spits over the rail. "The rain is not a room."
You heard him. The table, not the floor, and not a word of the hour where the water can listen.
"She stays tied till his name is read somewhere dry. Not my rule." He pats the rail like a horse that will not be ridden tonight.
Marsh puts a palm between the ledger and the deck. "Dry room," he says. "Her voice waiting. Not this boat, and not this fog."
You read his hour to the lane. The fog takes the words. Something matches your step and does not fall behind.
